description: Answer a question from long-term memory. Returns a synthesised answer and the memories it cites. Use this first when you need to know what is remembered about something. When the question is about a particular time, set `refers_to`.
name: memory_recall

filter.description: Narrows which memories are considered; every field set must match.

agent_id.description: Exact id of the agent that produced it.

file_path.description: File path, exact or as a path prefix.

folder.description: Folder, exact or as a path prefix.

kinds.description: Only these kinds of memory; empty means all.

observed_after.description: Only memories observed at or after this RFC 3339 time.

observed_before.description: Only memories observed before this RFC 3339 time.

repo.description: Exact repository, as `owner/name` or a URL.

sources.description: Only memories from these kinds of source; empty means all.

tags_any.description: Only memories carrying at least one of these tags.

url.description: Exact URL the memory was read from.

instructions.description: Optional extra instructions for how to answer (length, format, focus).

limit.description: Most memories the answer may cite.

question.description: The question to answer, in natural language.

refers_to.description: The local calendar dates the question is about, resolved against the Current Date & Time line. Set it whenever the question mentions or implies a time, in any language: "yesterday", "last Saturday", "in March", "kal", "pichle hafte", "el viernes". A single day has from == to. If a word can mean the past or the future (Hindi "kal"), cover both days. Prefer this over filter.observed_after/observed_before: those drop every memory recorded on another day, this only ranks the matching days first.
